what: A research-queue-dispatch cycle holds its concurrency group for ~75 min, so fire cycles cannot run more often than that and every extra manual/keeper dispatch queues behind the last. Measured on run 36798175014 (2026-10-01 00:50Z, event workflow_dispatch): 'Land the batch of runner results on main' 00:51:17Z -> 01:25:41Z (34 min), 'Grade and dispatch' 8 s, 'Land the liveness receipt' 4 min, 'Land the dispatch stamps on main' 01:29:57Z -> 02:06:51Z (37 min); job 00:50:31Z -> 02:06:54Z. Earlier runs the same shape: 36716391228 (12:41Z -> 14:05Z, 84 min), 36747172700 (16:50Z -> 17:36Z, 46 min). Each landing step opens an automation PR and polls it every 30 s until merged (commit-to-main VERIFY_MERGED, 30 min timeout), so the wait is merge-queue latency, not compute. Consequence: the dispatch itself takes seconds but fire cadence is bounded by landing latency; a cycle also fires at most --max-research-inflight 3 units. Options to cost out: (a) run the dispatch step FIRST and land stamps/results in a separate job so the next cycle does not wait on them; (b) land results and stamps in ONE PR; (c) drop VERIFY_MERGED for stamp PRs (stamps are idempotent data; the risk is a re-fire if the PR strands, which the liveness alarm would surface). Any of these touches the workflow or commit-to-main action, i.e. landing machinery: a human-read change.
